capacity_workload.name: mps_capacity_131072_sites_bond768_v1
capacity_workload.premise_established_note: No measured MPS shape is recorded as release-grade evidence that both exhausts one A800 and completes sharded at the same configuration, so the premise is unestablished and the gate must report it. What is on record is a development-smoke pair at one shape, 131,072 sites and bond dimension 768 at batch size one: a single-device CUDA out-of-memory record (benchmarks/results/local/mps_capacity_131072q_chi768_1xa800_oom_20260805.json, 75,148,300,800 peak bytes against an 85,093,777,408 byte device) and a 16-rank completion over two nodes (benchmarks/results/local/mps_capacity_131072q_chi768_16xa800_repeat_complete_20260806.json, world_size 16, local_world_size 8, node_count 2). Both records share the topology fingerprint c74a91e3a224a4dd414cfbfbcb31da7570880d42e6aa4eaccecf4b85427940a5, and both are development smoke: benchmark_evidence_class is local_non_release, claim_evidence_type is development_smoke, scalability_claim_allowed and release_gate_allowed are false on both, the single-device record carries no commit field, and neither carries a signed measured_production_run envelope, so neither is a premise this contract may build a release claim on. The completion record's single_gpu_capacity_failure flag is inherited from the failure record rather than re-measured in the same signed run. The peak the frozen body actually reaches was re-measured where the contract is measured now and is frozen as measured_single_device_peak_memory_bytes; the older artifact's reading travels in premise_provenance as a disclosed stale environment, because an inherited number cannot be the shape a freshly sealed baseline has to reproduce. The premise becomes established only by sealing a signed single_gpu_capacity_failure artifact and a signed multi_gpu_capacity_completion artifact at this frozen workload's digest, which is what the release gate requires.

premise_provenance.note: The only recorded multi-node MPS capacity completion was measured in a checkout whose revision is not in this repository's history, so its recorded commit cannot be resolved here, and it recorded a workload-body digest that differs from the body on disk. Two of its five sources, the raw log and the device telemetry, are absent. The premise producer therefore accepts the failure record it names, because that record and its digest are present and verified, and reports the rest as unverifiable rather than implying that it re-verified them. This drift is why the premise cannot be promoted on the strength of this artifact, and why a release run re-measures both legs at the digests frozen here. The single-device peak is the same story: the artifact records recorded_single_gpu_peak_memory_bytes from that other checkout, while measured_single_device_peak_memory_bytes is the peak the frozen workload body produces where the contract is measured now. The two readings differ because the environments differ and not because the shape does, which is why the stale reading is disclosed here and only the current one is the number a sealed baseline has to reproduce. The two digests differ for a second reason as well. rank_owned_initial_mps used to draw each distinct bond shape in the order the calling rank's own slice happened to visit it, so the tensor a wire received depended on where the rank boundaries fell and a sharded leg started from a different state than the single-device leg of the same frozen circuit; it now walks the shape sequence of the whole chain and keeps the wires the rank owns, so the initial state is a function of the wire's bonds alone. current_workload_body_sha256 is the digest of that revision.

capacity_workload.reverse_checkpoint_budget_note: The reverse tape is bounded at the frozen formula's value for the world size that ran, because the bound changes a rank's memory profile and not the arithmetic. Every measurement records the value it ran under, so a reader can tell whether a rank completed because the device holds the workload or because the tape was bounded.

single_gpu_baseline.rationale: One device has no ranks to shard one logical MPS across: its site ownership map is the whole state on one rank, so a world_size 1 artifact can never be a release payload and is read only as the provenance that shows the frozen workload exceeds one device. The strict promotion audit requires every file under benchmarks/results/scalability to be release-grade sharded scalability evidence, so the sealed baseline is written to its own candidate directory and is never promoted. The directory named here is where the capacity-failure role writes that sealed baseline; it currently holds nothing, and the only MPS single-device exhaustion measured so far is the development-smoke record digest-bound under frozen_evidence, which is not release-grade and cannot be read as the baseline.

workload_definition_sources.role: workload body: site count, bond schedule, rank boundary set and the circuit the capacity step trains

capacity_workload.workload_definition_sources_note: The launcher pins the site count and the body builds the circuit, so both files define the frozen workload and both digests are checked. Digesting only the launcher would let the work the contract claims to have measured change under a stable filename.
capacity_workload.workload_limitations: The frozen workload carries one independent trainable leaf per gate: a rotation of its own on each of the 16 rank-owning wires and a coupling of its own on each of the 15 sharded boundaries, so 31 leaves rather than the two shared scalars an earlier revision of this contract declared. The count is frozen here and is what capacity_workload.parameter_count states; the workload body computes it from the same site count and world size the rest of the contract is derived from, and the producer refuses a run whose body or measured ownership disagrees with it. One leaf per gate is the minimum that makes the per-parameter ownership the release payload reports a measured property rather than a consequence of the circuit: the engine assigns parameter index to rank index modulo world size, so a circuit with fewer leaves than ranks would leave surplus ranks owning no parameter and no optimizer state while the payload still called the optimizer update sharded. The workload remains a systems workload: it trains one Adam step against a single-site Z observable, so it measures whether one logical MPS state can be held and updated across ranks, and it is not an application-quality or expressivity claim. The probe blocker toy_circuit_parameters_only is a standing statement about the fixed five-wire circuit of the two-node transport probe artifact named in frozen_evidence, which is unchanged and still disclosed; it is not a statement about this frozen capacity workload.
capacity_workload.workload_sha256_note: The digest every capacity artifact must carry as workload_sha256. It is the digest of the frozen workload definition named by workload_definition_path, because that file is what fixes the site count, the bond dimension and the rank boundaries a completion artifact is compared against.

freeze_note: This contract was frozen before any MPS release run exists. It freezes the capacity workload (131,072 sites, maximum bond dimension 768, batch size one, one Adam step, approximate two-site gradient), the release topology (16 ranks over two hosts of eight devices each, which is the cluster that exists and the only sharded MPS configuration measured), the per-rank and MPS-specific artifact field contract, and the matched-speed acceptance thresholds. It deliberately freezes no matched-speed configuration ladder and no measured single-device speed floor, because no MPS matched-speed measurement of any kind has been taken: choosing timed configurations before a single MPS timing exists would freeze a protocol whose feasibility is unknown, which is how the tensor-network ladder came to contain an acceptance configuration that cannot run. The contract also records capacity_workload.premise_established=false: the only MPS single-device exhaustion and the only MPS sharded completion on record are development smoke (see capacity_workload.premise_established_note), so the release contract has no measured premise yet and the gate must report the missing premise rather than assume one. Every measured artifact this contract rests on is digest-bound under capacity_workload.frozen_evidence.

release_payload_envelope.note: The frozen MPS release world is 16 ranks, eight devices on each of two hosts, and the envelope enforces that bound both when a payload is sealed and when it is verified, so the contract can be satisfied only by a scope whose device counts include 16. The first frozen vocabulary had no such scope: SCHEDULED_SCALE stops at eight devices, which is one full host here, so this world was unsealable rather than merely unmeasured. API change proposal 065 added EvidenceScope.MULTI_NODE_SCALE, which carries exactly sixteen devices, and this contract was re-frozen against it. carriable is true because the envelope can now describe the frozen world, not because any run has satisfied it: no MPS measured_production_run artifact exists yet, and the gate still reports every other missing or unestablished element. The bound is stated here as four lists of numbers rather than derived at read time because a manifest is a frozen document; the gate derives the same bound by asking the envelope, and a disagreement means this note must be re-frozen.

runtime.accepted_backward_execution_statuses_not: The reverse-pass statuses the producer emits for a measured backward pass. The gate matches this list exactly rather than searching the label for 'executed' or 'production', because a projected or simulated reverse pass can name itself in the vocabulary of a measurement.
runtime.fallback_semantics_note: The single fallback declaration a release payload may carry. MPS training is approximate, so a payload that recomputed the same workload through a statevector path, a replicated per-rank autograd replay, or one rank holding a full local MPS would report numbers that are not sharded MPS evidence. The gate requires this exact string and an empty fallback_events list, because the sealed envelope records the fallback events the run observed.
runtime.launcher_note: The launcher is torchrun with one process per device, and it owns the process-group rendezvous: the executor does not initialize the group, so a rank that cannot reach its peers fails visibly instead of silently re-running the workload locally.

speed_workload.ladder_note: The matched-speed ladder is now frozen. configuration_ladder repeats the rungs ladder_definition_path defines so the release gate can read the timed shapes without executing code, and both the producer and the contract tests fail if the two copies disagree. Every rung is a reduced shape of the same capacity workload built by the same frozen body, at the same target world size, with the same trainable-leaf-per-gate parameterization, optimizer, gradient policy and reverse-tape rule, so a sharded leg of the acceptance rung is the capacity premise's own construction sharded rather than a second, unrelated circuit. The thresholds in this block are protocol rather than measurement: they are the levels a timed comparison must reach to be accepted, fixed before the legs ran so they cannot be chosen after the numbers are known.
speed_workload.measured_single_device_floor_note: The floor below was measured on one A800-SXM4-80GB before any release payload was sealed, under the frozen protocol: two warmup calls and ten measured calls, one optimizer step per call, the frozen reverse-tape rule (2 * (logical_mps_bytes // world_size) + 1 GiB) at world_size 1, and the frozen gradient policy. The ladder's cost is linear in the site count at a fixed bond dimension -- 0.51 s at 512 sites through 5.16 s at 8192 -- so the widest rung is the acceptance configuration and the ratio is not dominated by per-call overhead. The same final loss appears at every rung to six decimals, which is the arithmetic check that one construction was timed at five sizes rather than five different circuits. These readings come from an exploratory probe run outside the release producer (fq_mps_speed_probe.py, revision ac1043b6), so they freeze the protocol and the shapes; they are not release evidence and no payload rests on them. What a release payload must show is measured afterwards by benchmarks/mps_release_evidence.py, sealed, and read by the gate.
speed_workload.name: mps_matched_speed_v1
speed_workload.timing_unit: one full forward-and-reverse sharded MPS training step, measured end to end on the ranks it is sharded across

standing_blockers.name: host_staging_in_measured_region
standing_blockers.statement: The two-node transport probe staged ranks through host memory inside the measured region, so its timing is not device-to-device transport. A later transfer measurement can retire this blocker.

standing_blockers.name: toy_circuit_parameters_only
standing_blockers.statement: The probe exercised a toy parameterization rather than an application circuit. No measurement of this probe retires the statement, so it is recorded as a standing limitation of the transport evidence rather than as an outstanding task.

standing_blockers.name: two_node_pair_only_no_wider_topology
standing_blockers.statement: Only one pair of hosts exists here, so no measurement on this cluster can widen the topology. This is disclosed as a permanent boundary of the capability, not as a stage of its measurement, and it matches the frozen release topology of two nodes.

topologies.note: The measured cluster is one pair of hosts with eight A800 devices each, so the release topology is 16 ranks: eight per host, one rank per device, distributed across both hosts. Sixteen is not a preference but a floor for this contract: the frozen capacity workload holds 1,236,780,012,864 bytes of MPS state, which is 72.0 GiB on each of sixteen ranks against 79.25 GiB of usable device memory, and 144.0 GiB on each of eight, so eight ranks cannot hold the frozen shape at all. The frozen capacity workload fixes its 15 rank boundaries for that world size, so a different world size computes a different boundary set and a different topology fingerprint, and shrinking the world to fit a narrower evidence scope would mean shrinking the frozen workload, which would retire the capacity claim rather than certify it. No third host exists here, which is why the frozen topology is a pair of hosts rather than a ladder, and why the pair-only boundary is disclosed as a permanent limitation of the capability rather than as a stage of its measurement. The evidence envelope carries this world through EvidenceScope.MULTI_NODE_SCALE, added by API change proposal 065, so the topology is now sealable as well as frozen.
